title: the-cc-device
intention: Claude Code is a device in the Cairn rack at cairn/devices/cc/. Its shim receives MCP messages and notifies CC of them. It can tmux CC instances. Without this device, the cocoon strategy has no address to deliver work to, and a second Cairn instance cannot spin up its own CC.
why: The cocoon wraps CC (memory cocoon-settle-stages-around-cc), but the thing being wrapped has no address in the rack — no charter, no shim, no probes. Two filed tickets (superclaude-tmux-mode, cc-chat-pane-via-hook-append) are pieces that belong to a device that does not exist. Rob's research Cairn could not spin up a CC without this class definition.
traces_to: Telos 1 — inference compilation: the shim driving CC on idle is the system doing its own work.
Design: cocoon-settle-stages-around-cc — cheaper stages pre-process around CC.
Design: implementation-order-claude-first — CC is the first consumer of its own automation.
The ruled ladder: ground loop -> rack -> CC's shim -> Akien's shim -> web server -> librarian.

proves_green.proof_gate: tester runs probes via discover() — the device's probe folder loads with zero failures, the shim inherits BaseShim and arms on instantiation, and a message round-trips through the declared channel
proves_green.durability_gate: git commit — cairn/devices/cc/ and its contents are committed and pushed
proves_green.extra: the ground loop sees this device in its roster and fires its probes on each beat

falsifier.proves_red: RED on any of: (1) cairn/devices/cc/ does not exist with an intention+why.json charter, a shim inheriting BaseShim, and at least one probe; (2) the ground loop's discover() does not find the device and load its probes with zero failures; (3) a message sent through the shim's declared channel does not reach a running CC instance — verified by sending a test message and observing it arrive in the CC session.
falsifier.horizon: the device class exists and its shim is armed before superclaude-tmux-mode crosses to BUILDME, because tmux mode composes this device's shim

how: The device class at cairn/devices/cc/ with: (1) intention+why.json charter defining CC's role, what it owns, how it learns; (2) a shim inheriting BaseShim — an MCP server CC auto-connects to, routing messages from the bus and other devices; (3) probes the ground loop fires each beat; (4) instance 0 at ~/.cairn/devices/cc/0/. The device composes the superclaude launcher (lifecycle) and the BaseShim pattern (message routing).

decisions.text: The probe gets a real source instead of a key nothing sets. Measured 2026-10-13: CCShim.deliver (cairn/devices/cc/shim.py:45) persists each envelope as ~/.cairn/devices/cc/0/mail/msg-*.json and consume_mail deletes them, so the mail folder cannot count deliveries; nothing anywhere sets context['diagnostics_received']. The build, one commit '078476729bca: build — the shim keeps a ledger the probe counts': (1) in cairn/devices/cc/shim.py add module constant _LEDGER = _INSTANCE_ROOT / 'mail_ledger.jsonl' and a module function _ledger(event: dict, ledger: Path | None = None) that appends one JSON line (mkdir parents, open 'a'); deliver() appends {'event': 'delivered', 'id': msg_id, 'at': now.isoformat(), 'from': envelope.get('from', envelope.get('sender', 'unknown'))} after the os.replace; consume_mail() appends {'event': 'consumed', 'id': <the record's id>, 'at': <utc now iso>, 'session': os.environ.get('CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID', '')} for each message it removes. Both write to _LEDGER (module-level, so a proof can point it at a tmp path by setting shim._LEDGER and shim._MAIL_DIR; consume_mail and deliver read the module globals at call time). (2) rewrite cairn/devices/cc/probes/the_shim_delivers_mail.py: a function read_ledger(path: Path | None = None) -> list[dict] that reads the module-global LEDGER = address.instance_path('cc', 0) / 'mail_ledger.jsonl' when path is None (missing file -> [], a bad line skipped); _trigger(now, context) is True when any line has event 'delivered'; _carry returns {'delivered': n, 'consumed': n, 'sessions': sorted distinct non-empty sessions of consumed lines, 'delivery_times': the 'at' of the last three delivered lines}; _enough is True when consumed >= 3 and distinct sessions >= 2 (the ticket's own enough: three messages delivered across two separate CC sessions). PROBE keeps its why, to='harbor_master', body, horizon=100. Drop the diagnostics_received text from the docstring and say the ledger is what it reads. (3) new proof cairn/devices/cc/proofs/test_the_shim_delivers_mail.py, a script with a main() running these teeth over a tempfile.TemporaryDirectory, setting shim._MAIL_DIR, shim._LEDGER and the probe module's LEDGER to paths inside it and restoring them in finally: a_delivery_is_ledgered (deliver one envelope -> one 'delivered' line, trigger True), a_consumption_names_its_session (set CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID='s1', consume -> one 'consumed' line with session 's1'), enough_needs_two_sessions (three consumed under 's1' -> enough False; one more under 's2' -> enough True), an_empty_ledger_never_fires (no file -> trigger False, enough False). Imports of the probe and shim happen inside main(), never at module level. A module-level PROVES = {'078476729bca': {'1': 'a_delivery_is_ledgered', ...}} names the teeth. Proof: cairn/devices/cc/proofs/test_the_shim_delivers_mail.py. Then PROVEME --proven-by it, hollow seal, verdict, WATCHME (the probe is armed at its existing berth cairn/devices/cc/probes/the_shim_delivers_mail.py, receiver harbor_master as declared), PROVED. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09; approved thru PROVED (Akien 2026-10-12)

Folded into D1's build (the cc watch contract, ticket 802b3e49ae70, measured 2026-10-13): once repaired this ticket leaves FIXME and joins the standing population that cairn/devices/cc/proofs/test_cc_probes_report_to_the_watch.py reads, so (a) the rewritten PROBE also carries verb='watch' and carry=watch_carry('078476729bca', _carry, holds=_holds), importing watch_carry from cairn.tools.base.probe beside Probe, where _holds(context) reads the ledger and is False exactly when some 'delivered' id has no 'consumed' line and its 'at' is more than 24 hours old (mail delivered and never read is the failure), True otherwise including an empty ledger; (b) in the same build commit, through 'bin/cairn artifact write <ticket path> --verb cast', the ticket's watchme dict gains receiver {'what': 'harbor_master watch verb', 'in': 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'}; (c) in test_cc_probes_report_to_the_watch.py the tooth test_the_unreceivable_probes_sent_their_tickets_to_fixme keeps its name and asserts, for each id in UNRECEIVABLE, EITHER at FIXME with a kind 'watchme' fixme entry OR the id is among the ids _standing() returns (repaired: the other teeth then measure it). The new proof's PROVES also names a fifth tooth undelivered_mail_fails_after_a_day (a delivered line 25 hours old with no consumed line -> the watch_carry payload has holds False and a non-empty finding; consumed -> holds True). msg_id is the local variable deliver() already builds at cairn/devices/cc/shim.py:52 (f'msg-{UTC %Y%m%dT%H%M%S}-{uuid hex8}'), and the same string is the record's 'id' field written into msg-*.json (shim.py:54); consume_mail() takes the id for its 'consumed' ledger line from that loaded record's 'id' (record.get('id', p.stem)), so a delivered line and its consumed line carry the same id. Measured 2026-10-13. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The watchme receiver is written after BUILDME, exactly so: P=$(ls ~/dev/src/CairnCommons/tickets/078476729bca-*.json); python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(open(sys.argv[1])); d['watchme']['receiver']={'what': 'harbor_master watch verb', 'in': 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'}; json.dump(d, open(sys.argv[2],'w'), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)" "$P" $S/tk_0784.json; then bin/cairn artifact write "$P" --verb cast --why 'watchme gains its receiver (D3 b)' --from $S/tk_0784.json. receiver is a key inside the watchme dict, not a top-level ticket key, so plan_fields does not refuse it.
